Some people said: when fāḥisha (indecency) occurs in the definite form, it means adultery (zinā) and sodomy (liwāṭ); when it occurs in the indefinite form, it means all other sins and everything that is considered shameful; and when it is described by "clear" (mubayyina), it means the disobedience of a husband and the corruption of marital companionship. For this reason it is described as "clear", since it cannot be concealed, whereas adultery and other sins are things that are hidden and are not manifest. There is no doubt that the threat applies to what is hidden of it and what is apparent. Another group said: rather, His saying ﴿with a clear indecency﴾ encompasses all sins, and likewise "fāḥisha" in whatever form it occurs. Since the wives of the Prophet ﷺ were in the place of the descent of revelation and in the abode of Allah's commands and prohibitions, the matter was more binding upon them, and their status obliged them more than it obliged others. Therefore their reward and their punishment were doubled. The reference of "fāḥisha" is to adultery and other things.

Ibn Kathīr, Shibl and ʿĀṣim read "mubayyana" (with a fatḥa on the yāʾ). Nāfiʿ, Abu ʿAmr and Qatāda read it with a kasra on it. A group read "yuḍāʿif" with a yāʾ, attributing the verb to Allah the Exalted. Abu ʿAmr, as was transmitted from him, read "nuḍāʿif" with a damma on the nūn and "al-ʿadhāb" in the accusative. This is the reading of Ibn Muḥaysin, and it is a mufāʿala from one side, like "ṭāraqtu al-naʿl" and "ʿāqabtu al-liṣṣ". Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read "yuḍāʿif" with a yāʾ and an open ʿayn, and "al-ʿadhāb" in the nominative. Abu ʿAmr read "yuḍaʿʿif" with a shaddah on the ʿayn, in the intensive form, and "al-ʿadhāb" in the nominative. This is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Ibn Kathīr and ʿĪsā. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read "nuḍaʿʿif" with a nūn and a kasra on the doubled ʿayn, and "al-ʿadhāb" in the accusative. This is the reading of al-Jaḥdarī.

His saying ﴿ḍiʿfayn﴾ (twofold) means: the punishment becomes two punishments, that is, another punishment like it is added to the punishment of the rest of people. Abu ʿUbayda and Abu ʿAmr, as al-Ṭabarī transmitted from them, said: rather, two punishments like it are added to it, so that there are three punishments. Al-Ṭabarī judged this to be weak. It is also not sound, even though the wording allows it as a possibility. And the reward being "twice" disproves this view, because the punishment for indecency corresponds to the reward for obedience, and the reference of "that" (dhālika) is to the doubling of the punishment.

"Yaqnut" means: obeys and submits in servitude. This was said by al-Shaʿbī and Qatāda. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Abu ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read "yaqnut" with a yāʾ, and "taʿmal" with a tāʾ, and ﴿nu'tihā﴾ with a nūn. This is the reading of the majority. Abu ʿAlī said: "yaqnut" was attached to a pronoun; when it became clear that it was feminine, "taʿmal" was made to agree with the meaning. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read all three occurrences with a yāʾ, treating the first two as agreeing with the wording of "man". This is the reading of al-Aʿmash, Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ibn Thābit. Al-Aʿmash also read: ﴿then Allah will give her reward﴾.

"Al-iʿtād" means facilitating and preparing. "Al-rizq al-karīm" (the noble provision) is Paradise. It is also possible that in this there is a worldly promise, meaning that her provision in this world is upon Allah, and it is noble from the perspective that it is lawful, intended, and with Allah's pleasure in obtaining it. Some commentators said: the punishment with which she is threatened, twofold, is the punishment of this world and then the punishment of the Hereafter, and likewise the reward. This is weak, unless the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are such that the limits (ḥudūd) of this world do not avert from them the punishment of the Hereafter, as is the case with people generally, based on the ḥadīth of ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit. But this is a matter that was not transmitted concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, nor has its confirmation been preserved.

[p. 115] Then Allah addressed them, saying that they are not like any one of the women of their time or after, but rather they are superior, on condition of piety. This is because of what Allah granted them of companionship with the Messenger, peace be upon him, the greatness of their position with him, and the descent of the Qur'an concerning them. He specified "women" only because among those who preceded were Āsiya and Maryam. So consider this carefully. Qatāda has indicated this.

Then Allah forbade them from what was customary among the women of the Arabs, namely speaking to men in a soft, melodious voice. ﴿So do not be soft﴾ means: do not be gentle. Submission in speech may occur in the very words, their softness and their manner, even if the meaning is not suspicious. The Arabs use the word "khuḍūʿ" (submission) to mean inclination in amorous talk. From this is the saying of Layla al-Akhyaliyya when al-Ḥajjāj said to her: "Have you ever seen anything from Tawba that you disapproved of?" She said: "No, by Allah, O Amir; except that one day he recited a poem to me, and I thought from it that he had submitted to some matter. So I recited to him (this poem):

"And one with a need, we said to him: do not disclose it,
for as long as you live, there is no path to it for you."

End of the account.

Ibn Zayd said: "khuḍūʿ bi-l-qawl" is that which enters the hearts with amorous talk.

The majority read ﴿fa-yaṭmaʿa﴾ (so that he covets) in the accusative, as it is in the accusative by the fāʾ following a wish (tamannī). Al-Aʿraj and Abān ibn ʿUthmān read "fa-yuṭammiʿ" in the jussive, with a kasra for the sake of the meeting of two consonants. This is a pure fāʾ of conjunction (ʿaṭf), and the prohibition was without an apparent answer. The reading of the majority is more eloquent in the prohibition, because it indicates that the submission is due to coveting. Abu ʿAmr al-Dānī said: al-Aʿraj and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read "fa-yaṭmiʿa" with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and a kasra on the mīm.

"Al-maraḍ" (disease) in this verse: Qatāda said it is hypocrisy (nifāq). ʿIkrima said it is immorality (fisq) and amorous talk. This latter view is more correct, and hypocrisy has no place in this verse. "Al-qawl al-maʿrūf" (the known speech) is the proper speech that the Sharia does not reject and that souls do not deny.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verse 33:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:

﴿And remain in your houses, and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former time of ignorance (jahiliyyah). And establish prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with thorough purification.﴾

The majority (al-Jumhur) read the qaf with a kasra (waqarna / qirna). Nafi' and 'Asim read it with a fatha. As for the first reading, it may be from al-waqar (dignity, gravity): one says "waqqara yuqirru waqaran," and "qirna" is like "idna" (the form of the verb with the same pattern as "idna" from 'ada). It may also be from al-qarar (settling, staying): one says "qarartu bil-makan" (with a fatha on the ra) "aqirru," and the original form is "aqrarna," in which one ra was deleted for lightness, as they said in "zallaltu," "zaltu." They transferred its vowel to the qaf and dispensed with the alif. Abu 'Ali said: rather, it is explained by the ra being changed into a ya, its vowel transferred to the qaf, and then the ya deleted because it is sukun and the ra after it is also sukun.

As for the second reading, it is according to the language of the Arabs: "qarirtu (with a kasra on the ra) aqarru (with a fatha on the qaf) fi al-makan (in the place)." This is a dialect mentioned by Abu 'Ubayd in al-Gharib al-Musannaf, and mentioned by al-Zajjaj and others. Some denied it, among them al-Mazini and others. They said: "qarirtu" (with a kasra on the ra) is only said from "qurrat al-'ayn" (coolness of the eye). As for qarar (settling), it is only from "qarartu" (with a fatha on the ra).

'Asim read: "fi buyutikunna" (with a kasra on the ba'). Ibn Abi 'Ablah read: "waqrirna" with an alif of connection, and the first ra kasra. So Allah, exalted is He, in this verse commands the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to remain constantly in their houses, forbids them from display (tabarruj), and informs them that it is an act of the former time of ignorance.

al-Tha'labi and others mention that 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) used, whenever she recited this verse, to weep until her headscarf was wet. It is also mentioned that Sawdah was asked: "Why do you not perform Hajj and 'Umrah as your sisters do?" She said: "I have performed Hajj and 'Umrah, and Allah the Exalted has commanded me to remain (aqirra) in my house." The narrator said: "By Allah, she did not leave the door of her chamber until her funeral was carried out."

The qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

The weeping of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) was only because of her journey during the Battle of the Camel. At that time 'Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to her: "Allah has commanded you to remain (tuqirri) in your house."

And "tabarruj" is the display of adornment and affectation with it, and from it comes "al-buruj," because of its appearing and being exposed to the eyes.

The people differed concerning "al-jahiliyyah al-ula" (the former ignorance). Al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaynah said: it is the period between Adam and Noah (peace be upon them), which is eight hundred years, and blameworthy customs are related about them. Al-Kalbi and others said: it is the period between Noah and Abraham (peace be upon them). Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said: it is the period between Noah and Idris (peace be upon them), and he mentioned stories. A group said: it is the period between Musa and 'Isa (peace be upon them). 'Amir al-Sha'bi said: it is the period between 'Isa and Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon them). Abu al-'Aliyah said: it is the time of Sulayman and Dawud (peace be upon them), when a woman had a shirt of pearls that was not sewn at the sides.

The qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

What appears to me is that it refers to the ignorance that followed it, so they were commanded to move away from the conduct of that time, which is the conduct of the disbelievers before the Shari'ah, because they had no jealousy (ghayrah) and all women's affairs were without veiling. He made it "first" in relation to the state of Islam, and the meaning is not that there is another, different jahiliyyah. The term "jahiliyyah" has been applied to that period before Islam, so they said: "jahili" in reference to the poets. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said in al-Bukhari: "I heard my father in the jahiliyyah saying..." and so on, beyond this.

"Ar-rijs" is a term that applies to sin, to punishment, and to impurities and defects. So Allah removed all of that from the people of the household. "Ahl al-bayt" is in the accusative either as praise (madh), or as an addressed vocative (nida' mudaf), or by the implied verb "a'ni" (I mean).

The people differed concerning "ahl al-bayt": who are they? 'Ikrimah, Muqatil, and Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: they are specifically his wives; no man is among them. They held that "al-bayt" refers to the dwellings of the Prophet (ﷺ). Another group, which is the majority, said: the people of the household are 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with them). There are Prophetic hadiths on this. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'This verse was revealed concerning five: me, 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn.'" Among the proofs of the majority is His saying, "'ankum" (from you) and "yutahhirakum" (purify you) with the mim (the masculine plural), whereas if it were specifically for women it would have been "'ankunna" and "yutahhirukunna." What appears to me is that his wives are by no means excluded from this; the people of the household are his wives, his daughter, her sons, and her husband. This verse indicates that the wives are among the people of the household, because the verse is about them and addressed to them. As for the report that Umm Salamah said: "This verse was revealed in my house, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn, and he entered with them under a Khaybari cloak, and said: 'These are the people of my household,' reciting the verse, and said: 'O Allah, remove from them the impurity and purify them thoroughly.' Umm Salamah said: I said: 'And I, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'You are among the wives of the Prophet, and you are good.'" Al-Tha'labi said: they are the Banu Hashim. This indicates that "al-bayt" is meant as lineage, so al-'Abbas and his paternal uncles and their sons would be among them. Something similar was also narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam (may Allah be pleased with him).

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 34–35:

His Exalted and Majestic words:

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and the wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humbly submissive men and humbly submissive women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who remember Him—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

The sequence of these words indicates that "the People of the House" are his wives. According to the majority view, this is the beginning of an address, in which Allah the Exalted commanded the wives of the Prophet ﷺ—by way of admonition and enumerating a blessing—to remember what is recited in their houses. The word "remembrance" (al-dhikr) here may carry two intended meanings, both of which are admonition and enumeration of a blessing. One is that it means "remember" (udhkurna), i.e., that you should mention it and give it its due value, and reflect that one whose state is this should have his deeds beautified. The other is that it means "remember" in the sense of: preserve, recite, and keep it constantly on the tongues; as if he were saying: preserve the commands and prohibitions of Allah. That is what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah, and that leads you to uprightness. "Wisdom" (al-hikmah) is the Sunnah of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, upon the tongue of His Prophet, peace be upon him, without being in a recited Qur'an; it may also be understood as a description of the signs. In His words ﴿"Subtle"﴾ there is intimacy and enumeration of His blessings: that is, He is Subtle toward you in this blessing. In His words ﴿"Acquainted"﴾ there is a kind of warning.

As for His Exalted words: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾ up to the end of the verse. It was narrated from Umm Salamah that its occasion was that "she said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah the Exalted mentions men in His Book in everything, and does not mention us.' So the verse was revealed concerning that."

Qatadah narrated that "some women of the Ansar entered upon the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said to them: 'Allah has mentioned you in the Qur'an and has not mentioned the rest of the women with anything,' so the verse was revealed concerning that." It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "the wives of the Prophet said to him: 'Why does Allah the Exalted mention the believing men and not mention the believing women?' so the verse was revealed concerning that."

He began, Exalted is He, with mention of "Islam," which encompasses faith and the action of the limbs; then He mentioned "faith" specifically, as an emphasis and alert that it is the greatest part of Islam and its pillar. "Al-qanit" is the worshipper who is obedient. (p-120) "Al-sadiq" means: in what he has been pledged to, that he fulfills it and completes it. "Al-sabir" is one who is patient: against desires and in acts of obedience, in what is disliked and in what is liked. "Al-khashi'" is one who fears Allah, humbly submissive to His lordship, grave. "Al-mutasaddiq" is one who gives charity, obligatory and voluntary; it was said that it refers to the obligatory alone, but the first is more praiseworthy. "Al-sa'im" is likewise in the obligatory and voluntary. "Preserving the private parts" means protection from fornication and the like, and included with that is every act that leads to fornication or is on its path. In His words ﴿"al-hafizat"﴾ there is the omission of a pronoun indicated by what precedes it; its estimated form is: "al-hafizatuha" (those who guard them), and the same applies to "al-dhakirat" as well. "Forgiveness" is the covering of their sins and pardoning of them. "A great reward" is Paradise.

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and the wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humbly submissive men and humbly submissive women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who remember Him—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

**Commentary of Ibn ʿAṭiyya (al-Muḥarrar al-Wajīz) on Surah 33, verses 36–37:**

His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly gone astray into clear error.﴾

﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favor and you had bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you, so that there would be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them. And the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾

His saying: ﴿"Wa-mā kāna"﴾ (ﷻ). Its wording is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition and a forbidding of doing this. The expression "mā kāna" and "mā yanbaghī" and the like come to prohibit a thing and to rule that it shall not be. Sometimes the impossibility of that thing is rational, as in His saying: ﴿It was not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [al-Naml: 60]. Sometimes the knowledge of its impossibility is legal (sharʿī), as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him﴾ [al-Shūrā: 51]. Sometimes its prohibition is by a legal ruling, as in this verse. And sometimes it applies to recommended acts, as when you say, "It was not for you, so-and-so, to leave the supererogatory prayers," and the like.

The occasion of this verse, according to Qatādah, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, was that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed marriage to Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and she thought the proposal was for himself. When he made clear that he wanted her for Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, she disliked it and refused, so the verse was revealed, and Zaynab then submitted and married him." Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed on account of "Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, who offered herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he married her to Zayd ibn Ḥārithah. She and her brother disliked that and said, 'We wanted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),' so he married her to someone else. The verse was revealed on account of that," and then the two of them agreed to her marriage to Zayd.

And "al-khīrah" is a verbal noun meaning choosing. This verse is within His saying: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 6]. And His saying: ﴿And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 68] strengthens the view that "mā" there is a negation, not an object.

Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, Shaybah, al-Aʿraj and ʿĪsā read ﴿takūna﴾ with a *tāʾ* in agreement with the wording of *al-khīrah* (qirāʾah: a canonical recitation). ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read ﴿yakūna﴾ with a *yāʾ*, in agreement with the meaning of *al-khīrah*, since its feminine marking is not real. His saying in the other verse, ﴿They have no choice﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 68], without a feminine marker, strengthens this reading with the *yāʾ*.

Then Exalted is He threatened, and informed that whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray. This disobedience covers disbelief and what is less than it, and every disobedient person takes from error in proportion to his disobedience.

Then Exalted is He rebuked His Prophet (peace be upon him) by saying: ﴿And [remember] when you said﴾, the verse. The people differed in its interpretation. Qatādah, Ibn Zayd and a group of exegetes (mufassirūn), among them al-Ṭabarī and others, held that the Prophet (ﷺ) had felt admiration for Zaynab while she was in the marriage of Zayd, and he was keen that Zayd should divorce her so that he himself might marry her. Then when Zayd informed him that he wanted to separate from her, complaining of her harsh speech, disobedience to his command, verbal harm, and her pride in her nobility, he said to him: "Fear Allah," meaning regarding what you say about her, and ﴿keep your wife﴾. While he concealed his eagerness for Zayd's divorcing her, this is what he was concealing in himself, but he adhered to what was obligatory of enjoining good. They also said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared people's talk about this, so Allah rebuked him for all of this.

(p-122) Ibn Abī ʿAblah read: "mā Allāhu muẓhiruhu" (what Allah is to make manifest). Al-Ḥasan said: nothing was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) more severe for him than this verse. He and ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been concealing anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse because of how severe it was for him. Ibn Zayd related, in a similar account, that "the Prophet (ﷺ) asked for Zayd at his house, did not find him, and saw Zaynab uncovered, and she pleased him, so he said, 'Glory be to Allah, Turner of hearts.'" Many other things have been related about this story, the mention of which would be long, and what we have mentioned covers its meanings completely.

A group of those who interpret the verse held that there is no great reproach in it. ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly gone astray into clear error.﴾

﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favor and you had bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you, so that there would be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them. And the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾

His saying: ﴿"Wa-mā kāna"﴾ (ﷻ). Its wording is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition and a forbidding of doing this. The expression "mā kāna" and "mā yanbaghī" and the like come to prohibit a thing and to rule that it shall not be. Sometimes the impossibility of that thing is rational, as in His saying: ﴿It was not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [al-Naml: 60]. Sometimes the knowledge of its impossibility is legal (sharʿī), as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him﴾ [al-Shūrā: 51]. Sometimes its prohibition is by a legal ruling, as in this verse. And sometimes it applies to recommended acts, as when you say, "It was not for you, so-and-so, to leave the supererogatory prayers," and the like.

The occasion of this verse, according to Qatādah, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, was that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed marriage to Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and she thought the proposal was for himself. When he made clear that he wanted her for Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, she disliked it and refused, so the verse was revealed, and Zaynab then submitted and married him." Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed on account of "Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, who offered herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he married her to Zayd ibn Ḥārithah. She and her brother disliked that and said, 'We wanted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),' so he married her to someone else. The verse was revealed on account of that," and then the two of them agreed to her marriage to Zayd.

And "al-khīrah" is a verbal noun meaning choosing. This verse is within His saying: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 6]. And His saying: ﴿And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 68] strengthens the view that "mā" there is a negation, not an object.

Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, Shaybah, al-Aʿraj and ʿĪsā read ﴿takūna﴾ with a *tāʾ* in agreement with the wording of *al-khīrah* (qirāʾah: a canonical recitation). ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read ﴿yakūna﴾ with a *yāʾ*, in agreement with the meaning of *al-khīrah*, since its feminine marking is not real. His saying in the other verse, ﴿They have no choice﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 68], without a feminine marker, strengthens this reading with the *yāʾ*.

Then Exalted is He threatened, and informed that whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray. This disobedience covers disbelief and what is less than it, and every disobedient person takes from error in proportion to his disobedience.

Then Exalted is He rebuked His Prophet (peace be upon him) by saying: ﴿And [remember] when you said﴾, the verse. The people differed in its interpretation. Qatādah, Ibn Zayd and a group of exegetes (mufassirūn), among them al-Ṭabarī and others, held that the Prophet (ﷺ) had felt admiration for Zaynab while she was in the marriage of Zayd, and he was keen that Zayd should divorce her so that he himself might marry her. Then when Zayd informed him that he wanted to separate from her, complaining of her harsh speech, disobedience to his command, verbal harm, and her pride in her nobility, he said to him: "Fear Allah," meaning regarding what you say about her, and ﴿keep your wife﴾. While he concealed his eagerness for Zayd's divorcing her, this is what he was concealing in himself, but he adhered to what was obligatory of enjoining good. They also said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared people's talk about this, so Allah rebuked him for all of this.

He and ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been concealing anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse because of how severe it was for him. Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 38–44:

Allah the Exalted said:

﴿There is no fault upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him. That is the practice of Allah with those who passed on before, and the command of Allah is a decree determined.﴾ ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.﴾ ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance,﴾ ﴿and exalt Him morning and afternoon.﴾ ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He, toward the believers, Merciful.﴾ ﴿Their greeting, the Day they meet Him, will be "Peace," and He has prepared for them a noble reward.﴾

This is an address from Allah the Exalted to the entire Ummah. He informed them that there is no fault upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in obtaining what Allah has ordained for him and permitted him, namely the marriage to Zaynab after Zayd. Then He informed that this and its like is the oldest custom (sunnah) among the Prophets, that they should obtain what Allah has made lawful for them. Al-Tha'labi related from Muqatil and Ibn al-Kalbi that the reference is to Dawud (peace be upon him), when Allah joined him with the one who was tested by her. The word "sunnata" is in the accusative either as a verbal noun (masdar), or by supposing a verb whose estimate is "adhm" (adhere to) or the like, or as an incitement (al-igra'), as if he said: "upon him is the sunnah of Allah." "Those who passed on" (alladhina khalaw) are the Prophets, as evidenced by their being described afterward with the words: ﴿who convey the messages of Allah﴾. "The command of Allah" in this verse means: the things Allah commands, and the existing things that come from His command (p-125), so they are determined. His saying "qadaran" contains an omitted modifier, meaning: possessing measure and from measure. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "alladhina ballaghu risalati Allah" (those who conveyed the messages of Allah).

His saying: ﴿and fear none except Allah﴾ is an allusion to the first reproach concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) fear of people. Then He returned the whole matter to Allah, and that He is the Reckoner of all deeds and beliefs, and "sufficient is He; there is no god but Him." It is possible that "ḥasīban" means "muḥsiban," i.e., sufficient.

His exalted saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. In this verse Allah removed what had occurred in the hearts of the hypocrites and others after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Zaynab, the wife of his adopted son Zayd, because they had considered it grave that he should marry the wife of his son. So the Qur'an negated that image in regard to fatherhood. I know that Muhammad, in the reality of the matter, was not the father of any one of the men of his contemporaries. This verse was not intended to say that the Prophet (ﷺ) had no sons, which would require arguing about his sons by saying they had died, nor regarding al-Hasan and al-Husayn by saying they were infants. Whoever argues with that has interpreted the negation of fatherhood by this verse in a way other than what was intended.

Ibn Abi 'Abla and some people recited: "wa-lakin rasulu Allah" with the nominative, meaning: he is the Messenger of Allah. Nafi', Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, al-A'raj, and 'Isa recited "rasula" with the accusative, in coordination with "aba" (father). These read "wa-lakin" with the light pronunciation. A group recited "wa-lakinna" with the shadda on the nun, so "rasula" is accusative as the noun of "lakinna," and the predicate is omitted.

'Asim alone, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and al-A'raj with variation recited: ﴿"wa-khatama al-nabiyyin"﴾ with a fatha on the ta', meaning that they were sealed by him, so he is like the seal and the stamp for them. The rest and the majority recited it with a kasra on the ta', meaning that he is their finality, i.e., he came last of them. 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) related that he (peace be upon him) said: "I am the seal of a thousand prophets," with a fatha on the ta'. These expressions, among the scholars of the Ummah, earlier and later, are received in complete generality, explicitly requiring that there is no prophet after him. What al-Qadi Ibn al-Tayyib mentioned in his book named al-Hidaya, permitting the possibility of other readings in the wording of this verse, is weak. What al-Ghazali mentioned in this verse and this meaning in his book he named al-Iqtisad is, in my view, heresy and a vile approach to confusing the belief of the Muslims regarding Muhammad's (peace be upon him) sealing of prophethood. So beware, beware of it, and Allah is the Guide by His mercy. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "min rijalikum wa-lakin nabiyyana khatama al-nabiyyin" (…but our Prophet sealed the prophets). Al-Rummani said: by him, peace be upon him, the reform (al-istislah) was sealed; whoever is not reformed by him is despaired of being reformed.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾ is general, and what is intended here is His knowledge, blessed and exalted, of what He saw as most fitting for Muhammad (ﷺ) and what He decreed in the whole matter.

Then the Exalted commanded His servants to remember Him with much remembrance, and He made that without limit or measure, for its ease upon the servants and for the greatness of the reward in it. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: No one is excused from neglecting the remembrance of Allah except one whose intellect is overcome. He also said: "much" means that one never forgets Him. Abu Sa'id related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Remember Allah much, until they say: he is mad."

His saying: ﴿and exalt Him morning and afternoon﴾ intends: at all times, renewing the time at its two ends of day and night. Qatada, al-Tabari, and others said: the reference is to the two prayers of dawn and afternoon.

The author, Abu Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on him), said:

This verse is Medinan, so one who claims that prayer was first obligatory as two prayers at the two ends of the day should not rely on it, and the narration for that is weak. "Al-asil" is from the afternoon until night.

Then the Exalted enumerated to His servants His blessing in sending blessings upon them. Allah's blessing (salah) upon the servants is His mercy toward them, His blessing bestowed on them, and His goodly spreading toward us. The blessing of the angels is supplication for the believers. A group related that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Allah's blessing upon His servants?" (p-127) He said: "Subbuh, Quddus, My mercy has preceded My anger." Regarding the interpretation of this statement, it was said: all of this is the speech of Allah, and it is His connection to His servants. It was also said: "Subbuhun Quddus" is the speech of Muhammad (ﷺ), which he placed before a point with the wording that is Allah's blessing, which is: "My mercy has preceded My anger." He (peace be upon him) placed this first because he perceived from the questioner that he had imagined in Allah's blessing upon His servants an aspect unfitting for Allah the Exalted, so he put the glorification and exaltation of Allah before his reports.

His exalted saying: ﴿"liyukhrijakum"﴾ means: His blessing and the blessing of His angels, so that He may guide you and rescue you from disbelief to faith. Then the Blessed and Exalted informed of His mercy toward the believers, to reassure them.

His exalted saying: ﴿"yawma yalqawnahu"﴾ — it was said: on the Day of Resurrection, the angels greet the believer with peace, and its meaning is safety from every hated thing. Qatada (may Allah be pleased with him) said: on the Day of their entering Paradise, they greet one another with peace, meaning: we are safe and you are safe from every worry and fear. It was also said: the angels greet them on that day. As for "the noble reward," it is the Paradise of eternity in the neighborhood of Allah, blessed and exalted.

Then God the Exalted addressed the believers concerning the ruling on a wife who is divorced before consummation. Some people cited His saying: "then you divorced them," and the deferment implied by "then" (thumma), as evidence that divorce can occur only after a marriage, and that whoever divorces a woman before marrying her, even if he specifies her, does not incur it. But a great group of the people of knowledge said: the divorce of a specified person, whether an individual, a tribe, or a town, is binding before marriage. Among them are Malik and all his companions and a large number of the scholars of the Ummah. The majority of the reciters read: "touch them" (tamassuhunna), and Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Talha and Ibn Wathhab read: "tamasssuhunna" (with the two forms of the verb). The meaning of both is intercourse. **Commentary of Ibn ʿAtiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on Surah 33, verse 50:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified:

﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their bridal gifts (ujur), and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you as spoils (fay'), and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, not for the (other) believers. We have certainly known what We have imposed upon them concerning their wives and what their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty for you. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The majority of readers recited "al-lātī" with a *tāʾ* above (اللاتِي). Al-Aʿmash recited "al-lāyī" with a *yāʾ* below (اللايِي).

Ibn Zayd and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, in explaining His saying ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾, held that the meaning is that Allah, exalted is He, made lawful for him to marry any woman to whom he gives her mahr (bridal gift). Thus Allah permitted for him all women in this sense. He also permitted him ownership by right hand (milk al-yamin), and the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal uncles and aunts from among those who emigrated with him. He singled these out for mention to honour them and to draw attention. Among them, according to Ibn Zayd's interpretation, is what His saying covers: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful﴾. He also permitted for him the women who give themselves in gift, exclusively for him. So this, according to Ibn Zayd's interpretation, is an absolute permission regarding all women, except those within the prohibited degrees (dhawat al-maḥārim). Especially so, according to what al-Ḍaḥḥāk mentioned, that in the codex (muṣḥaf) of Ibn Masʿūd it reads: "and the daughters of your maternal aunts, and those who emigrated with you." (p. 131)

Then, after this, He said: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾ (Q. 33:51), meaning: from all these categories. Then the pronouns continue after that in a general sense, up to His saying: ﴿nor that you should exchange them for other wives﴾ (Q. 33:52). Thus this pronoun becomes detached from the first (reference), returning to his nine wives only, according to the difference of opinion regarding that.

Others besides Ibn Zayd interpreted His saying ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives, to whom…﴾ as referring to Ḥafṣa and ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them both, and those in his wedlock who had married with a mahr. They held that ownership by right hand came after (the first) lawful permission for him. They also held that Allah, exalted is He, permitted for him (ﷺ), along with those already mentioned, the daughters of his paternal uncles and aunts and of his maternal uncle and aunts, from among those who emigrated with him, and the women who give themselves in gift exclusively to him (ﷺ). Thus the matter, according to this interpretation, becomes more restricted for the Prophet (ﷺ). This interpretation is supported by what Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would marry whomever among the people he wished, and that was difficult for his wives. So when this verse was revealed and it was made unlawful for him (to marry) people except those who were named, his wives were pleased with that."

The Qāḍī Abū Muḥammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Because ownership by right hand is only relevant in rare circumstances, and the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal uncles and aunts are few, and the number of those he could marry from among them is limited in the view of his wives, especially since this is conditioned by the requirement of emigration (hijra). Likewise, women who give themselves in gift are few. Therefore his wives were pleased that the matter was restricted. Then His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾ (Q. 33:51) comes as a reference to those previously mentioned. Then His saying ﴿nor that you should exchange them for other wives﴾ (Q. 33:52) comes as a reference to his wives over whom the text previously made lawful (for him). Thus the discourse comes out coherent and consistent, more so than its consistency under the first interpretation. Al-ujūr means the mahr (bridal gifts).

His saying ﴿what Allah has returned to you as spoils﴾ means: He returned it to you from the war booty (ghanāʾim), intending: or to your community (ummatika), because it is fayʾ (returned property) to him. The origin of milk al-yamin is the fayʾ from the spoils of war, or what has been produced by descendants of those taken captive. Purchase from the people of war (al-ḥarbiyyīn) is like capture (al-sibāʾ), and capturing from the people of war is permitted. It is not permissible to take captive someone who has a covenant (ʿahd), nor to take him as property. This is called saby al-khibtha (the capture of a deceptive/treacherous kind).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles﴾ — it is narrated from Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him, and he excused me. Then this verse was revealed, and it made me unlawful for him, because I had not emigrated with him, and I was only among the Ṭulaqāʾ (those freed at the conquest of Makkah)."

The majority of readers recited ﴿"in wahabat"﴾ with a *kasra* on the *alif* (إنْ وهَبَتْ). This requires the matter to be a new (conditional) statement, meaning: if it occurs, then it is lawful for him. However, it has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "No woman was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except by a marriage contract or by ownership by right hand. As for a woman by gift, none of them was with him." Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Thaqafī and al-Shaʿbī recited ﴿"an wahabat"﴾ with a *fatḥa* on the *alif* (أنْ وهَبَتْ). In that case it refers to those women who gave themselves in gift before the revelation of the verse. The *kasra* of the *alif* fits with the interpretation of Ibn Zayd which we have mentioned earlier, and the *fatḥa* fits with the other interpretation. Whoever recited with the *fatḥa* said: the reference is to whichever women gave themselves to the Prophet (ﷺ) in general. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, as al-Ṭabarī reported: she is Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: she is Umm Sharīk.

Al-Shaʿbī and ʿUrwa said: she is Zaynab bint Khuzayma, Umm al-Masākīn. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr also said: Khawla bint Ḥakīm ibn al-Awqaṣ al-Sulamī. In the codex of Ibn Masʿūd it reads: "and a believing woman who gave herself in gift," without "in."

(p. 133) His saying ﴿exclusively for you﴾ means: the giving of themselves by women is a special privilege for him, "not permissible" for anyone else. So it is not permissible for a woman to give herself to a man. The people agreed that this is not permissible, except what has been narrated from Abū Ḥanīfa, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan and Abū Yūsuf, that they said: if she gives herself in gift and he calls witnesses upon himself with a mahr, then that is permissible.

The Qāḍī Abū Muḥammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Their statement is nothing but permitting the expression and the wording of "gift," for otherwise the acts they stipulated are the very acts of marriage (nikāḥ) itself. It appears from the wording of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with him, that the meaning of His saying ﴿exclusively for you﴾ is intended to cover this entire permission, because the believers were restricted to two, three or four (wives).

His saying "We have certainly known" (qad ʿalimnā) — the verse — means: We imposed upon them the guardian (walī), the witnesses, the mahr, and restriction to four. This was said by Qatāda and Mujāhid. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: it means two, three or four. His saying "so that there will not be" (li-kay lā yakūn) means: We made this clear and explained it in this way, so that there would be no difficulty for you and so that it would not be thought of you that you had sinned before your Lord in anything. Then He comforted all the believers with His forgiveness and mercy.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 51–52:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:

﴿You may defer whom you will of them, and you may take to you whom you will. And whomever you seek out from those you have set aside, there is no blame on you. That is more suitable so that their eyes may be comforted and they do not grieve, and they will all be content with what you have given them. And Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing.﴾ ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever Watchful over all things.﴾

﴿"Turji"﴾ means: you delay. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read "turji'" with a hamza. 'Asim (in the narration of Hafs), Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "turji" without a hamza. They are two dialects with the same meaning. ﴿"Wa tu'wi"﴾ means: you take in and draw near. Al-Mubarrad said: it is the transitive form of "raja yarju" (he hoped). You say: "raja al-rajulu wa arjaytuhu," meaning I made him one who has hope.

The meaning of this verse is that Allah, the Exalted, granted His Prophet latitude in what he does regarding the women. The pronoun in "minhunna" refers to those previously mentioned among the categories, concerning which the disagreement was mentioned.

This deferring and taking in may carry several meanings. Among them, regarding the division (of nights): you draw near whom you wish from yourself in the division due to her, and you defer whom you wish from you, you give more to whom you wish and less to whom you wish, with no blame upon you in that. When they know that this is the ruling of Allah, the Exalted, for you and His decree, their jealousy and rivalry will leave them, they will be content, and their eyes will be comforted. This is the interpretation of Mujahid, Qatada and al-Dahhak, because the cause of these verses was the jealousy that arose among the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, toward him, so he was distressed by that, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, granted him latitude and rebuked them with these verses.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn 'Abbas said: it concerns divorcing whom he wishes of those who were in his marriage and keeping whom he wishes. Ibn Zayd said: "The Prophet, peace be upon him, had resolved to divorce some of his wives, so they said to him, 'Divide (your nights) among us as you wish.' Among those he deferred were Sawda, Juwayriya, Safiyya, Umm Habiba and Maymuna, and he took in to himself 'A'isha, Umm Salama, Hafsa and Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with them all."

Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan said: the meaning is: in marrying whom he wishes of the women and leaving whom he wishes. Another group said: the meaning is: in taking in whom he wishes of those who gave themselves in marriage (al-wahibat) and deferring whom he wishes.

On every meaning, the verse signifies widening (of latitude) for him, peace be upon him, and permission. 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, recited this verse to me, I said: 'I see that your Lord is only hastening to fulfil your desire.'"

Hibat Allah, in his book "al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh," held that His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will﴾ abrogates His saying ﴿Women are not lawful to you﴾, and he said: "There is no abrogating verse in the Book of Allah that precedes the abrogated one except this." His argument is weak from several aspects.

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And whomever you seek out from those you have set aside﴾ may carry several meanings. One of them is that "man" is partitive, meaning: whomever you desire and whom your self seeks, from those you had set aside and deferred, there is no blame in returning him to yourself and taking him to you after his setting aside. A second aspect is that it strengthens and emphasizes His saying "You may defer whom you will and take to you whom you will," so that after it He says "And whomever you seek out from those you have set aside," and all of that is equal, with no blame upon you in any of it. This is like your saying: "Whoever met you from among those who did not meet you, all of them thankful to you," while you mean "whoever met you and whoever did not meet you." This meaning may apply to the matter of division, and it may apply to divorcing and keeping, and to the women who gave themselves; a group has held each of these.

The majority read ﴿"That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted"﴾ with the eyes in the nominative. Ibn Muhayşin read "an tuqirra" with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the qaf, with "a'yunahunna" in the accusative. His saying ﴿"bima ataytahunna"﴾ means: from yourself and your wealth. The majority of readers read ﴿"kulluhunna"﴾ in the nominative as an emphasis for the pronoun in "yarda'na." Al-Tabari allowed no other reading. Juwayrat ibn 'Abid read "kullahunna" in the accusative as an emphasis for the pronoun in "ataytahunna." The meaning is that they submit to Allah and His ruling. Previously they did not show tolerance toward one another out of jealousy, nor did they submit to the Prophet, peace be upon him, out of pride. Ibn Zayd and Qatada adopted this meaning.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ is a general statement, and the reference is to what was in the heart of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, of love for one person over another. Likewise the believers also enter into the meaning. His saying ﴿"Haliman"﴾ is an attribute that requires from Him, Blessed and Exalted, pardon and reassurance in this matter, since these are thoughts and reflections that a human being mostly cannot control.

The reports agree that he, peace be upon him, was just among them in the division until he died, and he did not act upon what was permitted to him with them, out of restraint of himself and taking the superior course. Except that Sawda gave her day to 'A'isha, seeking to gladden the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾. It was said, as we have mentioned: women had been made permissible for him apart from the nine who were with him, so the verse appears not to be connected to what precedes it. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatada, may Allah be pleased with them, said: when the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, abandoned them (in seclusion) for a month and took an oath regarding them, then came out and gave them the choice, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah rewarded them by forbidding him other women besides them, contenting him with them, and forbidding him to exchange them, and by this He abrogated what He had previously permitted him of widening regarding all women. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and 'Ikrima said: ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾ means: after the categories that were named. Whoever holds that the permission was absolute for him says here: ﴿Women are not lawful to you﴾ meaning: the Jewish women and the Christian women are not lawful to you. This interpretation is far-fetched, although it was narrated from Mujahid. Likewise some interpreted: nor that you exchange the Jewish and Christian women for Muslim women. This is the view of Abu Razin and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾ means: paternal aunts, maternal aunts and the like are not lawful to you. Along with that, he was commanded not to exchange his nine wives, and he was forbidden to divorce any of them and marry others. This was said by al-Dahhak. It was also said: "by taking the wife of a man who is in his marriage, i.e., he may not exchange her by taking another man's wife and giving him his own wife." Ibn Zayd said: this is something the Arabs used to do. This is a weak view, which al-Tabari and others rejected as an interpretation of the verse, and the Arabs never did this at all. As for the report from 'Uyayna ibn Hisn, that he entered upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, while 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, was with him, and said: "Who is this little red one?" The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "This is 'A'isha." 'Uyayna said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you wish, I will give up for you the chief of the Arab women in beauty and lineage" — this is not an exchange, nor did he intend that. He only belittled 'A'isha because she was a young girl, so he said this statement. Abu 'Amr, with a variant reading, read "tahillu" with a ta, meaning the group of women, while the rest read it with a ya below, meaning all women. Both are good readings, since the feminine form of the word "women" is not a true feminine.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And even if their beauty pleases you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: this was revealed concerning Asma' bint 'Umays, whose beauty pleased the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, when Ja'far ibn Abi Talib died leaving her, so he wished to marry her. In this phrase, ﴿even if their beauty pleases you﴾, there is evidence for the permissibility of a man looking at the woman he wishes to marry. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said to al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, who wished to marry a woman: "Look at her, for that is more likely to create harmony between you both." He said to another man: "Look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the Ansar." Al-Humaydi said: this means: [that they have] yellowness. Sahl ibn Abi Hathma said: "I saw Muhammad ibn Maslama pursuing Buyayta bint al-Dahhak on a donkey-cart among the carts of Madina, so I said to him: 'Do you do this?' He said: 'Yes. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "When Allah places in the heart of one of you the proposal to a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her."'"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾. "Ma" is in the nominative position as a substitute for "al-nisa'", and it may be in the accusative position as an exception, though the accusative has weakness. It is also possible that "ma" is verbal (masdariyya), with the implied meaning: "except the ownership of your right hand," in the sense of "possessed," and it is in the accusative position because it is an exception from a different category than the first. "Al-raqib" is an intensive form (fa'il) in the sense of active participle (fa'il): i.e., one who watches.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 51–52:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:

﴿You may defer whom you will of them, and you may take to you whom you will. And whomever you seek out from those you have set aside, there is no blame on you. That is more suitable so that their eyes may be comforted and they do not grieve, and they will all be content with what you have given them. And Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing.﴾ ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever Watchful over all things.﴾

﴿"Turji"﴾ means: you delay. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read "turji'" with a hamza. 'Asim (in the narration of Hafs), Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "turji" without a hamza. They are two dialects with the same meaning. ﴿"Wa tu'wi"﴾ means: you take in and draw near. Al-Mubarrad said: it is the transitive form of "raja yarju" (he hoped). You say: "raja al-rajulu wa arjaytuhu," meaning I made him one who has hope.

The meaning of this verse is that Allah, the Exalted, granted His Prophet latitude in what he does regarding the women. The pronoun in "minhunna" refers to those previously mentioned among the categories, concerning which the disagreement was mentioned.

This deferring and taking in may carry several meanings. Among them, regarding the division (of nights): you draw near whom you wish from yourself in the division due to her, and you defer whom you wish from you, you give more to whom you wish and less to whom you wish, with no blame upon you in that. When they know that this is the ruling of Allah, the Exalted, for you and His decree, their jealousy and rivalry will leave them, they will be content, and their eyes will be comforted. This is the interpretation of Mujahid, Qatada and al-Dahhak, because the cause of these verses was the jealousy that arose among the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, toward him, so he was distressed by that, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, granted him latitude and rebuked them with these verses.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn 'Abbas said: it concerns divorcing whom he wishes of those who were in his marriage and keeping whom he wishes. Ibn Zayd said: "The Prophet, peace be upon him, had resolved to divorce some of his wives, so they said to him, 'Divide (your nights) among us as you wish.' Among those he deferred were Sawda, Juwayriya, Safiyya, Umm Habiba and Maymuna, and he took in to himself 'A'isha, Umm Salama, Hafsa and Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with them all."

Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan said: the meaning is: in marrying whom he wishes of the women and leaving whom he wishes. Another group said: the meaning is: in taking in whom he wishes of those who gave themselves in marriage (al-wahibat) and deferring whom he wishes.

On every meaning, the verse signifies widening (of latitude) for him, peace be upon him, and permission. 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, recited this verse to me, I said: 'I see that your Lord is only hastening to fulfil your desire.'"

Hibat Allah, in his book "al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh," held that His saying ﴿You may defer whom you will﴾ abrogates His saying ﴿Women are not lawful to you﴾, and he said: "There is no abrogating verse in the Book of Allah that precedes the abrogated one except this." His argument is weak from several aspects.

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And whomever you seek out from those you have set aside﴾ may carry several meanings. One of them is that "man" is partitive, meaning: whomever you desire and whom your self seeks, from those you had set aside and deferred, there is no blame in returning him to yourself and taking him to you after his setting aside. A second aspect is that it strengthens and emphasizes His saying "You may defer whom you will and take to you whom you will," so that after it He says "And whomever you seek out from those you have set aside," and all of that is equal, with no blame upon you in any of it. This is like your saying: "Whoever met you from among those who did not meet you, all of them thankful to you," while you mean "whoever met you and whoever did not meet you." This meaning may apply to the matter of division, and it may apply to divorcing and keeping, and to the women who gave themselves; a group has held each of these.

The majority read ﴿"That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted"﴾ with the eyes in the nominative. Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified:

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are permitted for a meal, without waiting for its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that would cause discomfort to the Prophet, and he would be shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah.﴾

This verse contains two matters: the first is the etiquette concerning food and sitting, and the second concerns the veil (hijab).

As for the first, the majority of the commentators (mufassirun) hold that its occasion was: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he held a wedding feast (walima) for her and invited the people. When they had eaten, a group remained seated in a part of the house. This was burdensome to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he went out so that they would leave with his departure. He passed by the rooms of his wives, then returned and found them still in their places, with Zaynab in the house with them. When he entered and saw them, he withdrew. At that, they left. Anas said: 'I was informed, or I informed him, of their departure, so he came. When he reached the room, he let the curtain fall between me and him, and he entered. The verse was revealed because of that.'" Qatadah and Muqatil, in the book of al-Tha'labi, said: this occasion took place in the house of Umm Salama. The first is more well known. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: it was revealed concerning some of the believers who used to watch for the Prophet's meal (ﷺ), entering upon him before the food was ready until it was prepared, then they would eat and not leave. Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim said: this is an etiquette which Allah, exalted is He, taught to the burdensome guests (al-thuqala'). Ibn Abi 'A'isha said in the book of al-Tha'labi: "It is enough of a description of the burdensome guests that the Law did not tolerate them."

As for the verse of the veil, Anas ibn Malik and a group said: its occasion was the matter of sitting in Zaynab's house, the story mentioned just above. Another group said: rather, it was in the house of Umm Salama. Mujahid said: the verse of the veil was revealed because of that. 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) and a group said: the cause of the veil was the words of 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), and that he spoke to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) repeatedly, asking that he veil his wives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not do so, and 'Umar kept pressing. Then Sawda went out at night for her need, and she was a woman who was tall among women. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) called out to her: "We have recognized you, O Sawda," out of eagerness for the veil. Zaynab bint Jahsh said to him: "We are amazed at you, O son of al-Khattab! You are jealous over us while revelation descends in our houses?" 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) kept pressing until the verse of the veil was revealed.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I agreed with my Lord in three matters: among them the veil, the station of Ibrahim, and ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]." The hadith.

The author, the Qadi Abu Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on him), said:

It was the custom of the people, when they had a feast or something similar, that whoever wished would come early to the house of the invitation, waiting for the food to be cooked and ripened in conversation and companionship. Likewise, when they finished, they would sit in the same manner. So Allah, exalted is He, forbade the believers from such things in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the prohibition covered all the believers. The people adhered to the etiquette which Allah, exalted is He, set for them in this matter. He forbade them from entering without permission at the time of eating, not before it, in waiting for the food to ripen.

"Nazirin" means "waiting" (muntazarin). "Inahu" is the verbal noun of "anā al-shay'u ya'nī", when a thing is finished and its time has come (anā/yan'ā). From it is the saying of the poet:

"Death has labored over him on a day, and it has come to its time (anā), and for every pregnant woman there is a completion."

The majority read the nun of "inahu" with a fatha, and Hamza and al-Kisa'i inclined it (imala).

Then He emphasized the prohibition and restricted the time of entry to being when permission is given. Then He commanded, after the meal, that their gathering disperse and scatter.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor seeking to remain for conversation﴾ is coordinated (atf) with His saying: ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾. "Ghayr" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) from the kaf and mim in "lakum", meaning: "not waiting for it and not seeking to remain for conversation." Ibn Abi 'Abla read "ghayri" with a kasra on the ra'. Its permissibility is by way of the estimate: "not waiting for it, you [yourselves]." Al-A'mash read "inahu" as the plural of "inan" with a long vowel after the nun. A group read "fa-yastahyi" by pronouncing the kasra on the ya' before the sukun, and a group read "fa-yastahi" with a sukun on the ya' without a kasra before it. His saying: ﴿But Allah is not shy of the truth﴾ means: abandoning the saying of the truth does not occur from Him. Since that occurs among humans from the cause of shyness, He negated from Allah, exalted is He, the cause which necessitates it among humans.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you ask them for something﴾ up to the end of the verse is the verse of the veil. "Mata'" (goods/utensils) is general to all that can be requested according to the custom of dwelling and neighbourhood, from household vessels and all the other utilities for religion and worldly life. ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾ means: from the thoughts that come upon women concerning the matter of men.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ up to the end of the verse. It is narrated that it was revealed because "some of the Companions said: 'If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dies, 'A'isha will be married [to someone],' and this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was hurt by it." Thus Ibn 'Abbas referred to him only as "some of the Companions," and Makki related from Ma'mar that he said: "It was Talha ibn 'Ubayd Allah."

The Qadi Abu Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

How excellent is the understanding of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both). But this, in my view, does not hold true regarding Talha; may Allah protect him from it. And it is narrated: "A man from the hypocrites said, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Umm Salama after Abu Salama, and Hafsa after Khunays ibn Hudhafa: 'What is the matter with Muhammad, marrying our women? By Allah, if he dies, we will draw lots for his wives with arrows.' So the verse was revealed concerning this." Allah forbade marrying his wives after him and gave them the ruling of mothers. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and the Arabs apostatized, then returned, 'Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl married Qatila bint al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had married her but had not consummated the marriage. This was grievous to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), and he was disturbed by it. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: "Easy, she is not one of his wives. He did not give her the choice, nor did he draw a veil over her, and he has already separated her from himself by returning her to her people." So Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was calmed. And 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) decided that none should attend the funeral of Zaynab bint Jahsh except a close relative (dhu mahram) of hers, out of regard for the veil. Asma' bint 'Umays then guided him to her covering in the bier with a dome, and informed him that she had seen this in the land of Abyssinia, so he adopted it. It is also narrated that this was done at the funeral of Fatima, daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ).

(p-١٤٣)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, or what their right hands possess. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it﴾, the verse… It is a threat, a rebuke (tawbikh) and a warning for those addressed by the allusion in the verse before it, from among those referred to in His saying: ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], and those referred to in His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53]. So it was said to them in this verse: indeed Allah knows what you conceal of these beliefs and disliked thoughts, and will recompense you for them. Then, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned the permission regarding those of the relatives He named, since the circumstances of human beings require the entry of those mentioned, their frequent coming and going, and the safety of their souls from the matter of desire, because souls shun those who are within the prohibited degrees (dhawat al-mahARim). Among these are the fathers, the sons, the brothers, their sons, and the sons of the sisters.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor their women﴾ includes the sisters, the mothers, all other relatives, and those who are connected to them among those who are attributed to them. This is the view of a group of the people of knowledge. The specification of the attribution in the phrase ﴿"their women"﴾ supports their view. Ibn Zayd and others said: what is meant is all believing women, and the specification of the attribution is only in terms of faith.

As for His saying: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Nur: 31], a group said: it refers to female slaves (imaa') only, not male slaves (ʿabid). Another group said: it refers to both male and female slaves. Then this second group differed. One faction said: it refers only to the male slaves they own, not to those owned by others. Another faction said: rather it refers to all slaves, whether they are in their ownership or in the ownership of others. As for the mukatab (a slave who has contracted to purchase his freedom) who has what he can pay with, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that the veil be lowered before him. Umm Salama did this with her mukatab Nabhan. This was reported by al-Zahrawi.

A group said: the paternal uncles are included under "fathers." al-Sha'bi and Ikrimah said: He did not mention them because they may describe (their women) to their sons, and likewise the maternal uncles. They disliked that a woman should remove her khimar (headcover) in the presence of her paternal or maternal uncle.

The commentators differed about the aspect in which blame is lifted by this verse. Qatada said: it is the hijab, meaning that these categories are permitted to enter upon the women without the veil and to be seen by them. Mujahid said: it concerns lifting the jilbab (outer garment) and displaying adornment.

(p-١٤٤)When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the concession for these categories, and the permission was complete, He connected the command to fear Him with a conjunction of sentence to sentence. This is in the utmost eloquence and conciseness, as if He had said: confine yourselves to this, and fear Allah in it, lest you transgress it to something else. Then, blessed and exalted is He, issued a warning with His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾.
