As for His saying: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Nur: 31], a group said: it refers to female slaves (imaa') only, not male slaves (ʿabid). Another group said: it refers to both male and female slaves. Then this second group differed. One faction said: it refers only to the male slaves they own, not to those owned by others. Another faction said: rather it refers to all slaves, whether they are in their ownership or in the ownership of others. As for the mukatab (a slave who has contracted to purchase his freedom) who has what he can pay with, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that the veil be lowered before him. Umm Salama did this with her mukatab Nabhan. This was reported by al-Zahrawi.

A group said: the paternal uncles are included under "fathers." al-Sha'bi and Ikrimah said: He did not mention them because they may describe (their women) to their sons, and likewise the maternal uncles. They disliked that a woman should remove her khimar (headcover) in the presence of her paternal or maternal uncle.

The commentators differed about the aspect in which blame is lifted by this verse. Qatada said: it is the hijab, meaning that these categories are permitted to enter upon the women without the veil and to be seen by them. Mujahid said: it concerns lifting the jilbab (outer garment) and displaying adornment.

(p-١٤٤)When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the concession for these categories, and the permission was complete, He connected the command to fear Him with a conjunction of sentence to sentence. This is in the utmost eloquence and conciseness, as if He had said: confine yourselves to this, and fear Allah in it, lest you transgress it to something else. Then, blessed and exalted is He, issued a warning with His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 56–58:

The Most Exalted said:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who abuse believing men and believing women without their having earned it have certainly borne the burden of slander and manifest sin.﴾

This verse is one by which Allah honoured His Messenger ﷺ, mentioned his rank with Him, and cleared away the evil act of one who entertained an evil thought concerning his wives and the like.

As for His saying: ﴿"yuṣallūn" (send blessings)﴾, one group said: the pronoun in it refers to Allah and to the angels. This is a statement from Allah, the Exalted, by which He honoured His angels, so it is not subject to the objection that arose from the saying of the orator before the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray," whereupon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Evil is the orator you are," – they said: because it is not permissible for any human to join the mention of Allah the Exalted with another in a single pronoun, whereas Allah may do of that whatever He wills. Another group said: there is an elision in the speech, its implied sense being: "Indeed Allah sends blessings upon the Prophet, and His angels send blessings," and what was omitted is indicated by what is apparent in the statement; there is no joining in one pronoun in the verse, and that is permissible for humans to do. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not say "Evil is the orator you are" for this meaning; he said it only because the orator paused at "and whoever disobeys them" and stopped briefly. Among what supports this is that in the words of the Prophet ﷺ in the Sunan of Abu Dawud: "So he joined the mention of Allah the Exalted with His Messenger in one pronoun." Among what supports the first view is that in the Book of Muslim: "Evil is the orator you are; say: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger.'" This may be understood to mean that when he corrected him for his pause and said to him "Evil is the orator you are," he afterwards amended his whole speech for him, because separating the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted from the pronoun of another is without doubt preferable; so he said to him "Evil is the orator you are" for the place where he corrected him in the pause, and directed him to the preferable course in separating the two pronouns, although joining them is permissible.

The reading of the majority is ﴿wa-malā'ikatahu﴾ with the *ta'* in the accusative, as a conjunction upon the pronoun in the verb. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, read it in the nominative, as a conjunction upon the position before the entry of *inna* (the place of the subject), and this requires consideration.

The blessing of Allah the Exalted is His mercy and blessing, and the blessing of the angels is supplication and glorification. Blessing upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at all times is, among the obligatory acts, of the obligation of the emphasised sunnahs, which it is not correct to abandon, and none neglects it except one in whom there is no good. The Prophet ﷺ, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Increase your blessings upon me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day."

Its form is what has been transmitted from him ﷺ in the book of al-Tabari, by way of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: that when this verse was revealed, some of the Companions said to him: "This is the greeting upon you, O Messenger of Allah, which we already know; so how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham, and have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You had mercy upon Abraham and the family of Abraham among the worlds; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'" In some of the narrations there is addition and omission; this is its meaning.

Ibn 'Abbas... [note: the text is continuous here]

Al-Hasan read: "O you who have believed, so send blessings upon him," and this *fa'* strengthens the meaning of a condition, i.e., "Allah has sent blessings, so you too send blessings," just as you say, "I have given you, so take." In the reading of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud): "Send blessings upon him as Allah has sent blessings upon him, and greet him with peace."

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed those who abuse Allah and His Messenger⦆ – the verse – the majority said its meaning is: by disbelief, and by attributing to Him a companion, a son, or a partner, and by describing Him with what does not befit Him. There is a hadith: "Allah said: 'My servant abused Me by saying: He has a son; and he denied Me by saying: He will not be resurrected.'" 'Ikrimah said its meaning is: by image-making and by bringing about an act that only Allah does, namely carving and creating images; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said: "Allah curses the image-makers." Another group said that this is by an elision of a qualifier, its implied sense being: "those who abuse the friends of Allah."

Harming the Messenger ﷺ is by what hurts him of sayings in more than one sense, and of deeds as well. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: it was revealed concerning those who taunted him when he took Safiyya bint Huyayy.

The Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

And the taunting concerning the appointment of Usama is also a harm to him.

As for His saying [la'anū] (they were cursed), its meaning is: they were removed from every good.

As for harming believing men and believing women, it is likewise by evil deeds and sayings, by slander and by fabricated, gross lies. It is related that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said one day to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Indeed I recited last night this verse, ﴿And those who abuse believing men﴾ – the verse – and I was alarmed by it. By Allah, I shall strike them and rebuke them." Ubayy said to him: "You are not one of them, O Commander of the Faithful; you are only a teacher and a corrector." Abu Hatim mentioned that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: "Indeed those who abuse believing men and believing women," then said to Ubayy, may Allah be pleased with him: "How do you recite this verse?" and he recited it as 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, had recited it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verse 59:

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He:

﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments (jalabib) over themselves. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Since it was the custom of Arab women to be lax regarding the meaning of covering, and they used to uncover their faces as slave women do, and this was an invitation to men to look at them and to let their thoughts wander toward them, Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger ﷺ regarding them to have them draw the jalabib over themselves, so that their covering would be achieved; thus whoever was amorous or young would refrain from opposing them.

It is narrated that in Madinah there were people who used to sit on the raised paths (al-su'udat) to see women, to confront them and to seek to seduce them, and the verse was revealed because of that.

And al-jilbab (jilbab): a garment larger than the khimar (head-covering). It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, and from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that it is the rida' (outer wrap). People differed regarding the manner of drawing it over oneself. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ubayda al-Salmani said: it is that the woman wraps it so that nothing of her appears except one eye through which she sees. Ibn 'Abbas also said, and Qatada: it is that she wraps it above the forehead and fastens it, then folds it over the nose; even if her two eyes appear, it covers the chest and most of the face.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known﴾, meaning: in general, by distinction, so that they are not mixed with slave women. When they are recognized, they will not be met with harm from those who oppose them, out of regard for the rank of freedom. The meaning is not that the woman should be recognized so that it is known who she is. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw a slave woman who had veiled herself, would strike her with his whip, safeguarding the dress of free women.

The remainder of the verse is encouragement, gentleness, an incitement to repentance, and an inducement to hope for the mercy of Allah; and in it is reassurance for women regarding abandoning the jalabib before this commanded matter.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 60–62:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:

﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in the city do not desist, We will surely set you upon them; then they will not remain as your neighbours therein except for a little.﴾ ﴿Cursed; wherever they are found, they shall be seized and slain with a [thorough] slaying.﴾ ﴿This is the way of Allah with those who passed away before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾

The lam in "la-in" (la'in) is the one announcing the coming of an oath, and the lam in "la-nughriyannaka" (lanughriyannaka) is the lam of oath. Allah, blessed and exalted, threatened these categories in this verse, and He coupled His threat with a sign of their continuing in refusing to desist. A group said: these categories did not desist, and Allah the Exalted did not carry out this threat against them; this verse is therefore evidence for the invalidity of the view that the threat is executed in the Hereafter. Another group said: these categories did desist, and all of them concealed their matter and held back; what remained of their matter, Allah the Exalted executed a threat against in correspondence to it, such as the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of praying over them, and other things the Messenger of Allah ﷺ inflicted upon the hypocrites: the humiliation in expelling them from the mosque, and what was revealed concerning them in the Surah of Repentance (Bara'a), and other things. Thus they did not comply with desisting entirely, nor was the threat fully carried out against them.

"Al-munafiqun" (the hypocrites) are a category that shows faith but does not conceal disbelief within. "Those in whose hearts is a disease" and "the agitators in the city" are people from among the hypocrites who used to speak of the Arabs invading Madina and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be overcome, and similar things with which they unsettled the souls of the believers. It is possible that these categories are distinct from one another, and it is possible that they are included within the general body of the hypocrites, but He specified these two groups, though the word "hypocrisy" already encompasses them, as a warning about them, a means of scattering them, and a belittling of them.

"Nughriyannaka" (we will set you upon them) means: We will urge you against them after they have been identified to you. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We will empower you over them." Qatada said: "We will guard you with them." His saying "thumma la yujawiruunaka" (then they will not remain as your neighbours) means: after the setting-upon; for you will expel them by fear and killing. "Illa qaliilan" (except for a little) may mean: except for a brief neighbourhood or a brief time, and it may mean: except for a small number, as if he said: except for a few. His saying "mal'unina" (cursed) may be in the accusative as a form of censure, as al-Tabari said; it may be a substitute for "aqilla'a" (a few) which we estimated earlier in one of the interpretations; and it may be a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the pronoun in "yujawiruunaka," as if he said: they will be removed from the city cursed. [When the estimate of "la yujawiruunaka" as "yantifuna" (they will be removed) was established, this was good.] Al-La'na (curse) is distance. "Thuqifu" (wherever they are found) means: they are confined and overpowered. "Ukhidhu" (they shall be seized) means: they are taken captive, and the akhidh (captive) is the prisoner; from it is the saying of the Arabs: "more of a liar than the akhidh al-Sabhan." The majority of readers recited "wa-qutthiluu" (and slain) with a doubled ta', and the verbal noun following it supports this. A group recited it with a single ta' (qutilu), and the verbal noun, in this reading, is irregular. Al-A'mash said: everything in the Qur'an other than this place is "qutiluu" with a single ta'.

His, the Exalted, saying: "Sunnata Allah" (the way of Allah) [al-Ahzab/Ghafir: 85] is in the accusative as a verbal noun; it may also be taken as an incitement from afar. "Alladhina khalaw" (those who passed away) are the hypocrites of earlier nations. His saying: "wa-lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi tabdila" (and you will not find any change in the way of Allah) means: no one who could make a change that is firmly established; so the change of the disobedient and disbelievers is excluded from this, while what Allah changes from one sunna to another by abrogation is excluded from it as well.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verse 63–68:

(p-150) His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying:

﴿They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah." And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire,﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper.﴾ ﴿The Day their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ ﴿And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our chiefs, and they misguided us from the [right] way.﴾ ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse."﴾

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the time of the Hour, when it would occur, and he did not answer concerning that at all, and the verse was revealed," commanding that knowledge of it be referred to Allah, since it is among the keys of the unseen which Allah, the Exalted, has reserved the knowledge of for Himself. Then He warned the one who knows of its nearness in His saying: ﴿And what would make you know?﴾ the verse... That is: one should be wary. "Qarīban" (near) is an adverb whose form is one whether singular or plural, masculine or feminine; had it been an adjective for "al-sā'ah" (the Hour), it would have been "qarība" (near, feminine). Then Allah, the Exalted, warned the disbelievers of a punishment from which they will have no protector or helper.

His saying "yawma" (the Day) may be connected to what precedes it, with its governing verb being "yajidūn" (they will find); this is the view of al-Ṭabarī. It may also be that its governing verb is "yaqūlūn" (they will say), and it is then an adverb of the saying.

Al-Jumhūr (the majority) read ﴿"tuqallabu wujūhuhum"﴾ with the passive form, with a damma on the tā' and a shadda on the lām, which is open. Abū Ḥaywa read "taqallabu wujūhuhum" with a fatḥa on the tā', meaning "tataqallabu" (they are turned over). Ibn Abī 'Abla read "tataqallabu" with two tā's. Khārija and Abū Ḥaywa read "nuqallibu" with the nūn. 'Īsā ibn 'Umar al-Kūfī read "tuqallibu" with a damma on the tā' and a kasra on the lām, with "al-wujūh" in the accusative, meaning the Blaze turns their faces over. So on that Day they will wish for faith and obedience to Allah and His Messenger, when wishing will not benefit them.

Then they sought refuge in complaining about their great ones, that they had misled them. The majority of people read ﴿"sādatanā"﴾, which is the plural of "sayyid" (lord). Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, and Ibn 'Āmir alone among the Seven, and Abū 'Abd al-Raḥmān, Abū Rajā', Qatāda, and the common people in the Congregational Mosque of Basra read "sādātanā," as a plural of the plural. "Al-sabīlā" is a second object, since "aḍalla" (to lead astray) is transitive by means of the hamza, while "ḍalla" transitively takes one object. It is the way of faith and guidance. Then they called for Allah to double the punishment for the great ones who misled them, that is: for themselves and for those whom they misled. 'Āṣim, Ibn 'Āmir, Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, and al-A'raj, according to one of the two reports from him, read ﴿"la'nan kabīran"﴾ with a bā', from "kibar" (greatness). The rest and the majority read "la'nan kathīran" with a thā' of three dots, and "kathra" (abundance) is more fitting to the meaning of a curse than "kibar," that is: curse them many times over.

"Qarīban" (near) is an adverb whose form is one whether singular or plural, masculine or feminine; had it been an adjective for "al-sā'ah" (the Hour), it would have been "qarība" (near, feminine). Then Allah, the Exalted, warned the disbelievers of a punishment from which they will have no protector or helper.

His saying "yawma" (the Day) may be connected to what precedes it, with its governing verb being "yajidūn" (they will find); this is the view of al-Ṭabarī. It may also be that its governing verb is "yaqūlūn" (they will say), and it is then an adverb of the saying.

Al-Jumhūr (the majority) read ﴿"tuqallabu wujūhuhum"﴾ with the passive form, with a damma on the tā' and a shadda on the lām, which is open. Abū Ḥaywa read "taqallabu wujūhuhum" with a fatḥa on the tā', meaning "tataqallabu" (they are turned over). Ibn Abī 'Abla read "tataqallabu" with two tā's. Khārija and Abū Ḥaywa read "nuqallibu" with the nūn. 'Īsā ibn 'Umar al-Kūfī read "tuqallibu" with a damma on the tā' and a kasra on the lām, with "al-wujūh" in the accusative, meaning the Blaze turns their faces over. So on that Day they will wish for faith and obedience to Allah and His Messenger, when wishing will not benefit them.

Then they sought refuge in complaining about their great ones, that they had misled them. The majority of people read ﴿"sādatanā"﴾, which is the plural of "sayyid" (lord). Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, and Ibn 'Āmir alone among the Seven, and Abū 'Abd al-Raḥmān, Abū Rajā', Qatāda, and the common people in the Congregational Mosque of Basra read "sādātanā," as a plural of the plural. "Al-sabīlā" is a second object, since "aḍalla" (to lead astray) is transitive by means of the hamza, while "ḍalla" transitively takes one object. It is the way of faith and guidance. Then they called for Allah to double the punishment for the great ones who misled them, that is: for themselves and for those whom they misled. 'Āṣim, Ibn 'Āmir, Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, and al-A'raj, according to one of the two reports from him, read ﴿"la'nan kabīran"﴾ with a bā', from "kibar" (greatness). The rest and the majority read "la'nan kathīran" with a thā' of three dots, and "kathra" (abundance) is more fitting to the meaning of a curse than "kibar," that is: curse them many times over.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verses 69–71:

(p-151) His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying:

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses; but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ ﴿He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment.﴾

Those who abused Moses were a people from the Children of Israel. People differed concerning the harm (idhaya) from which Allah cleared him. One group said: it is the story of Qarun and his placing of the adulterous woman (al-mar'a al-baghiyya) to claim against Moses, then Moses's clearing her and exposing Qarun's collusion. The story has already been mentioned in the discussion of Qarun. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is that Moses and Harun, peace be upon them both, went out from the open ground of al-Tih to a mountain, and Harun died there. Moses came alone, and a people said: he killed him. So Allah sent angels who carried Harun, peace be upon him, and paraded him among the tribes of the Children of Israel. They saw a great sign which indicated the truthfulness of Moses, peace be upon him, and there was no trace of [killing] on him. It is narrated that he came back to life and informed them of his affair and of Moses's innocence. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayra, and a group said: it is what is contained in the hadith of the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, and Moses, peace be upon him, would conceal himself greatly and hide his body. So a people said: he has a hernia, or is leprous, or has some defect. Then Moses bathed one day alone and placed his garments on a rock, and the rock fled with his garments, and Moses followed it saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' So he passed in his pursuit by an assembly of the Children of Israel, and they saw him free of what had been suspected of him..." – the hadith in its entirety, related by al-Bukhari. So Allah cleared him of what they said.

(p-152) And "al-wajih" means the one honored in face. The majority read: ﴿"and he was in the sight of Allah"﴾, and Ibn Mas'ud read: "and he was 'Abd Allah." Then Allah enjoined the believers to speak appropriate words, and that encompasses all good. 'Ikrima said: He meant: "There is no god but Allah," and al-sadad encompasses all of this. Although the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that He only pointed to what would be contrary to the harm that was said concerning the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the believers. Then Exalted Allah promised that He rewards for appropriate speech with the amendment of deeds and the forgiveness of sins. The rest of the verse is clear.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 33, verse 72–73:

His words, may He be exalted and glorified:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.﴾ ﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and believing women. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The people differed concerning the amanah (trust). Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is the trusts of wealth, such as deposits and the like. It is also narrated from him that it encompasses all the obligations (al-fara'id), and the most severe of them is the trust of wealth.

A group, which is the majority (al-jumhur), held that it is everything a person is entrusted with, of command and prohibition, and matters of religion and worldly affairs. So the whole Shari'ah is a trust. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Among the trust is that a woman be trusted with her private part." Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The ghusl of janabah is a trust." The meaning of the verse is: We offered to these great created beings that they bear the commands and prohibitions, and that they be subject to reward if they do well and punishment if they do evil. So these created beings refused and were apprehensive.

It is possible that this occurred through a perception Allah created in them, and it is possible that this offering was made to those among them who are angels. It is narrated that they said: "My Lord, leave me subjected to whatever You wish, obedient in it, and do not entrust me to my own judgment and action, and I do not desire a reward." "And man bore the trust," that is, he undertook to carry out its right, and in that he is a wrongdoer to himself and ignorant of the extent of what he has entered into. This is the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jubayr. Al-Hasan said: "and bore it" means he betrayed it, and the verse concerns the unbeliever and the hypocrite.

The qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

And the disobedient according to their degree.

Ibn 'Abbas and his companions, al-Dahhak, and others said: "the man" (al-insan) is Adam. He undertook the trust, but a day had not passed for him before he committed the sin by which he was expelled from the Garden. It is narrated that "Allah, blessed and exalted, said to him: O Adam, I offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it. Will you bear it with what it entails?" He said: "And what does it entail?" He said: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished." He said: "Yes, I have borne it." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "So there passed for him only the time between the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer before he disobeyed his Lord."

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas said: "the man" is the son of Adam, Qabil, who killed his brother, and he had undertaken for his father the trust that he would guard the family after him. Adam, peace be upon him, had travelled to Makkah in a long narration which al-Tabari and others mention.

Some of them said: "the man" is the whole species, and this is good given the generality of the trust.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of the verse is: We offered the trust, in Our prohibitions and Our commands, to these created beings, and they upheld its command and obeyed in what We charged them with, and they shrank from bearing the blame for disobeying Us. And man bore the blame in what We charged him with of Our commands and Our law. And "man," according to his interpretation, is the unbeliever and the disobedient.

This verse is consistent with His words: ﴿We came, obedient﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. According to the first interpretation we related, His words ﴿We came, obedient﴾ [Fussilat: 11] are an answer to a command they were given, and this verse is a refusal and apprehension (p-154) concerning a matter that was presented to them and they were given the choice in it. It is narrated that "Allah offered the trust to these created beings and they refused. When Allah, blessed and exalted, offered it to Adam, peace be upon him, he said: I will bear it upon my ear and my neck. Allah said: Indeed I will help you. I have placed a veil over your sight, so close it to what is not lawful for you, and a garment over your private part, so do not uncover it except for what I have made lawful for you." Many things have been related in this sense which I have left out for brevity, due to their lack of soundness.

Some said: the verse is figurative, meaning: when we measure the weight of the trust against the strength of the heavens, the earth and the mountains, we see that they cannot bear it, and that if they could speak they would refuse it and be apprehensive. He expressed this meaning by His words "We offered," as you say: "I presented the load to the camel and it refused it," and you mean by that: I measured its strength against the weight of the load and found that it falls short of it.

His words, may He be exalted, ﴿So that Allah may punish﴾: the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), because man did not bear it in order that punishment should befall; rather he bore it, and the matter turned out to be that the hypocrite and the polytheist would be punished, and that He would turn in forgiveness to the one who believed. Al-Jumhur read "yatuba" in the accusative, coordinated with His words ﴿"li-yu'adhdhiba"﴾; al-Hasan read it in the nominative, as a resumption and new clause. The rest of the verse is clear.

Completed, by the help and success of Allah, is the tafsir of Surat al-Ahzab.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
